newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Anderton challenges NZ First on National coalition.
newsitem.headline: Anderton challenges NZ First on National coalition.

text.p: The Alliance on Monday called on New Zealand First to rule out a coalition with National, predicting that if it did not do that its slide in the polls could continue.

"If New Zealand First won't rule out National, the Alliance calls on all New Zealand First supporters to reconsider their support for that party because it would almost certainly mean a continuation of National in government," Alliance leader Jim Anderton said.
"New Zealand First supporters should decide whether supporting New Zealand First is worth the possibility of a further three years of National government.
"That will mean a continuation of market rentals for state housing, a continuation of the commercialisation of the public health system and continued underfunding of education."
In last night's One Network News-Colmar Brunton poll, NZ First plunged five points to 14 percent support while National was boosted by a five-point rise to 40 percent.
Act broke the 5 percent barrier for the first time in the Colmar Brunton poll and its rating would give it six seats in Parliament.
Labour was up two points to 18 percent and the Alliance was unchanged on 15 percent.
The Christian Coalition, one of National's potential supporters in the next Parliament, slipped to just below the threshold and was on 4.5 percent.
Anderton interpreted NZ First's drop to its policy of refusing to rule out a coalition deal with any party after the election.

Although he appears to be shifting away from National and moving closer to Labour, NZ First leader Winston Peters still maintains that any decisions on coalition agreements will be made by a vote of his new caucus.
Anderton said if NZ First did not "unequivocally eliminate National as a coalition partner" voters should recognise that only the Alliance and Labour were an alternative to National.
